headline: You have spreading redness around your wound; please contact your surgical team today.

reasons.finding: Spreading beyond incision line as a broad patch around the lower end
Redness extends beyond incision line, mild swelling, edges intact, small dark crusts present
Compared to baseline pale skin, now redness spreading

steps: Call your surgical team today to report the spreading redness.
Check your temperature twice daily and note any fever of 38°C or higher.
Keep the wound clean and dry; avoid scratching or applying creams.
If you develop fever, worsening pain, or the wound opens, seek urgent care.
message_to_team: Hello, I am day 4 after abdominal surgery. I have noticed spreading redness around the lower part of my incision, with warmth and tenderness, though my temperature is 37.2°C and there is no discharge or foul smell. Please advise if I need to be seen today.

second_check.note: Spreading redness with warmth and tenderness suggests possible wound infection requiring prompt surgical review.

photo_words: The wound is closed with a vertical line of interrupted stitches. Redness extends beyond the incision line as a broad patch around the lower end; a distance is not clearly measurable. The skin in that red area looks mildly swollen, and the wound edges are not apart. Small dark crusts sit along
